data.title: Northrop Grumman advances Sentinel nuclear missile toward flight test
data.description:
Northrop Grumman (NOC) and the U.S. Air Force assembled a fully integrated inert Sentinel missile at Vandenberg Space Force Base, clearing a key technical milestone ahead of flight testing planned for 2027.

The missile was assembled vertically in its operational orientation during a four-month exercise known as Pathfinder. The demonstration tested whether the program team could transport, handle, stack and integrate the missile safely at a launch site.

 

 

Northrop (NOC) said the exercise included all missile stages, propulsion elements, the protective shroud and related components. Engineers also tested specialized transportation vehicles, mobile crane operations and interfaces on the launch pad.

The inert missile was subsequently taken apart after completion of the exercise.

Design review, flight test schedule

Separately, Northrop Grumman and the Air Force’s 719th Test Squadron completed the first flight-test Critical Design Review.

The review determined that the missile’s design maturity and hardware testing met Air Force requirements for performance, safety and scheduling. The company said Sentinel remains on pace for its first flight test in 2027.

“This vertical assembly demonstrates the momentum toward test launching Sentinel in 2027 and having missiles on alert by the early 2030s,” said Amanda Davis, vice president and general manager of strategic deterrent systems at Northrop Grumman.

The milestones provide evidence that Sentinel is progressing from digital design and component testing toward a physically integrated weapon system. For Northrop (NOC) investors, successful execution is important because Sentinel is expected to remain a major long-duration defense program as the Air Force replaces the aging Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile system.

Northrop (NOC) leads a nationwide Sentinel team of more than 500 suppliers and over 10,000 workers. The planned system is intended to remain operational through 2075, giving the company potential exposure to decades of development, production, maintenance and modernization spending.

The latest achievements do not eliminate the program’s execution risks. Assembling an inert missile demonstrates that its components and ground procedures fit together, but a live flight test will be a more demanding measure of propulsion, guidance, control and overall system performance. Maintaining the 2027 test schedule will therefore be an important milestone for investors monitoring the program.

Modernizing nuclear triad

Sentinel is intended to modernize the land-based portion of the U.S. nuclear triad, which also includes submarine-launched missiles and nuclear-capable aircraft.

Northrop (NOC) said the program is advancing toward initial operational capability in the early 2030s. The company and the Air Force are also working on missile testing, launch infrastructure, supply-chain readiness and the equipment needed to place the weapon in operational silos.

The Pathfinder exercise brings Sentinel closer to that goal, although the program still must complete flight testing and other qualification work before missiles can be placed on alert.

data.title: Carlyle-backed Avenrock Energy to buy Parallax Energy, expanding oil and gas ​reach in Canada
data.description:
Carlyle Group (CG) said Monday its newly formed Canadian company Avenrock Energy agreed to acquire Parallax Energy from Carnelian Energy Capital, establishing a significant new light oil platform in Western Canada.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but Reuters reported ​the total enterprise value of the deal ​was ~C$1B and said Parallax's gross production ‌totals ⁠20K boe/day.

Parallax owns and operates a 75% working interest in a portfolio of exploration and production assets in Alberta's East Shale Duvernay, maintaining ~300K gross acres and a substantial production base focused predominantly on light oil and natural gas liquids, as well as an extensive owned infrastructure network.

The deal is the second in the past year ​by Carlyle's (CG) energy business, which last ​year bought Kiwetinohk Energy for ~C$1.4B.

data.title: Ocean Power Technologies issues going-concern warning, launches strategic review
data.description:
Ocean Power Technologies (OPTT) fell 3.6% post-market Monday after saying it initiated a strategic alternatives review following its quarterly results and a leadership shakeup, according to a 10-Q filing.

The company said its board initiated the review to identify opportunities to increase growth, expand market access, and strengthen its financial position; Bowen is serving as financial advisor, and no timetable has been established for the review.

The move comes as Ocean Power (OPTT) reported its FQ1 loss widened to $10.5M from $7.4M in the year-earlier quarter, while its per-share loss remained at $1.28.

The company said current conditions raise "substantial doubt" about its ability to continue as a going concern, with the ability to continue as a going concern dependent upon operations in the future and obtaining the necessary financing to meet its obligations and repay its liabilities.

Ocean Power (OPTT) shares slumped 14.5% in regular trading Monday after the company announced leadership changes including the departure of CEO Philipp Stratmann, to be succeeded as acting CEO by previous chief executive Tracy Pagliara.

data.title: Westaim to rebrand as “Aventus Capital” with the AVTS ticker
data.description:
• The Westaim (WED:CA) announced on Monday that it will change its name to Aventus Capital, effective September 17, 2026.
  • Its shares are expected to begin trading on the TSX Venture Exchange under the new AVTS ticker.
  • The company is also rebranding Arena Investors, LP as CCaventus Asset Management LP, its institutional asset management business.
  • The rebrand does not change the company’s share capital, and existing share certificates remain valid.
  • CEO Cameron MacDonald said the new brand reflects Aventus’ evolution into an integrated insurance and alternative asset management platform.

data.title: Gold slides as surging oil prices, Treasury yields bolster Fed rate-hike expectations
data.description:
Gold futures fell Monday to their lowest in more than a month as surging energy prices and bond yields continued to boost expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates this week, outweighing safe-haven demand generated by escalating geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East.

Brent crude oil jumped to nearly $110/bbl in the first trading session following Saudi Arabia's closure of its critical pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz due to damage from missile attacks, extending last week's ~9% surge after fighting escalated between the U.S. and Iran.

Although Treasury yields pulled back after the 10-year touched 5% for the first time in three years on Monday, precious metals have struggled since last week's hotter-than-expected inflation data that saw the U.S. Producer Price Index rise 5.4% in the 12 months through August after climbing 4.8% in July.

The dollar rose to a two-week high, making greenback-priced bullion ​more expensive for holders of other currencies.

Traders are now pricing in a 93% chance of a rate hike at this week's Fed policy meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

"The possibility of more interest rate hikes by major central banks, amid higher oil prices and geopolitical developments, could further support yields and keep gold under strain," Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage said in a note.

The Fed meeting is the main event for gold, which could be pulled down by any hawkish signals at the press conference, but "any soft messaging from the Fed may ease tightening bets and help gold recover," Sage wrote.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for September delivery dipped 1.3% to $4,310.00/oz, and front-month Comex September silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slumped 1.6% to $63.513/bbl, the lowest settlement value for the respective metals since August 6 and August 7.

data.title: TORM announces secondary public offering of class A common shares by selling shareholder
data.description:
TORM (TRMD) announced on Monday the commencement of a secondary public offering of 9M of the company's Class A common shares by OCM Njord Holdings, a company indirectly owned by funds managed by Oaktree Capital Management, L.P., and its affiliates.

The company said that the selling shareholder expects to grant the underwriter a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1.35M class A common shares offered in this offering. 

The firm added that the selling shareholder beneficially owns approximately 20% of the company's Class A common shares before this offering. The company is not selling any Class A common shares and will not receive any proceeds from the sale of its Class A common shares by the selling shareholder. 

Source: press release

data.title: Boeing lands up to $552.1M Navy contract modification for MQ-25 aircraft
data.description:
• The Boeing (BA) received a not-to-exceed $552.1M undefinitized U.S. Navy contract modification for MQ-25A Stingray aircraft.
  • The deal covers three Lot One aircraft and long-lead components for three Lot Two aircraft.
  • Moreover, the Navy will initially commit $164.4M, including $100M from fiscal 2025 funds and $64.4M from fiscal 2026 funds.
  • The work is expected to be completed by July 2031.
  • Naval Air Systems Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Planet Ventures proposes five-for-one share consolidation
data.description:
Planet Ventures (PNXPF) announced on Monday that it intends to consolidate its common shares based on five pre-consolidation shares for every one post-consolidation share.

The company highlighted that the consolidation is intended to make it more attractive to potential new investors.

The consolidation was approved by the board of directors of the company in accordance with the articles of the company but remains subject to the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange. 

The company said it will not be changing its name with the consolidation.

Source: press release

data.title: Rubrik rallies 16% amid peer gains
data.description:
Shares of Rubrik (RBRK), a cloud-based data protection and cyber resilience company, jumped nearly 16% on Monday, closing at $100.20 and adding $13.55 per share.

The gain came as the broader market retreated, with major indices finishing in negative territory. However, cybersecurity peers showed notable strength. For example, stocks like Zscaler and Okta posted sharp advances of just over 16% and nearly 12%, respectively.
